Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, os
for m in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pymupdf','PIL']:
 print(m, importlib.util.find_spec(m))
print('tools', [p for p in ['/usr/bin/gs','/usr/bin/pdftoppm','/usr/bin/pdftotext','/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/utility/.runtime/ghostscript-9.55.0/bin/gs'] if os.path.isfile(p)])
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs'); p.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
for i,page in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=page.extract_text()
 (p/f'page-{i+1:02}.txt').write_text(t)
 print(f'PAGE {i+1}: {len(t)} chars')
(p/'manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+page.extract_text() for i,page in enumerate(r.pages)))
print((p/'manuscript.txt').read_text()[:29000])
PY"

strengths: QuEST addresses an important deployment problem with a practical combination of synthetic calibration, temporal quantization, and selective teacher-guided finetuning. Updating at most 7% of LDM-4 parameters is an appealing design.

The W4A4 improvements on unconditional generation are substantial: Table 3 reports FID reductions from EfficientDM's 10.60 to 5.64 on LSUN-Bedrooms and from 14.34 to 11.76 on LSUN-Churches, while the evaluated PTQ baselines fail.

Evaluation spans unconditional, class-conditional, and text-to-image generation, with 50,000 samples for the main LDM evaluations and 10,000 COCO prompts for Stable Diffusion. The qualitative examples support the narrower claim that recognizable W4A4 Stable Diffusion images are achievable.

The activation-distribution and sensitivity analyses provide useful empirical motivation. Table 7 demonstrates improved W4A8 FID alongside reduced calibration time relative to Q-Diffusion. The manuscript supplies a code link, cites its datasets and baselines, and reports several implementation details.
weaknesses: The theoretical justification is substantively flawed. Section 2.3.1 expands MSE with respect to the final output; this loss is exactly quadratic, so its second-order Taylor expansion remains exact for arbitrarily large output perturbations. Large perturbations therefore do not establish the claimed breakdown. Furthermore, Equation 5 replaces Equation 10's epsilon-based Hessian term with an output-residual quadratic without justification. Theorem 2.2 does not establish that weight finetuning, particularly of the selected subset, is sufficient. These issues undermine the theoretical contribution, although they do not invalidate the empirical results.

The distinctive benefit of selective and progressive optimization is insufficiently isolated. EfficientDM already provides data-free finetuning, and Appendix A acknowledges earlier timestep grouping. Table 7 supports adding the proposed components, but lacks comparisons against equally sized alternative layer subsets or joint versus progressive training. Its W4A8 setting also leaves the mechanisms behind the headline W4A4 gains insufficiently tested.

The efficiency comparison omits the closest finetuning baseline, EfficientDM. Table 7 demonstrates lower calibration time than Q-Diffusion but higher memory use: 12,450 versus 10,334 MB. Without comparable measurements for EfficientDM and actual inference latency, the broader efficiency advantage remains only partially established.

Generation-quality evidence is uneven. On ImageNet W4A4, QuEST has worse sFID and IS than EfficientDM: 7.93 versus 7.75 and 202.45 versus 250.90, respectively. The slightly better FID is difficult to interpret given the manuscript's own concerns about that metric. Stable Diffusion is evaluated quantitatively only through CLIP Score, which does not establish visual fidelity or diversity; complementary quality evaluation would strengthen this central result.

Reporting needs greater precision for reproducibility and comparison. The 'full 4-bit' description should prominently acknowledge the 8-bit attention matrix multiplications and first/last layers disclosed on page 2. Exact selected layer lists, quantizer granularity and initialization, classifier-free guidance settings, and the definition of Table 7's 'Baseline' are insufficiently specified. These are addressable reporting concerns, distinct from the theoretical and experimental shortcomings above.
